summary: The core is mostly generic jtframe parts (vtimer, scroll, tilemap, objdraw) set up with parameters, and its module split is the usual main/video/scroll/text/obj/colmix framework layout, not one module per board chip. Its strongest hardware signal is the priority mixer: it drives the 29.14K priority PROM, which MAME leaves unused, through a specific address-pin mapping. That same mixer also has a debug-selectable model transliterated from MAME's screen_update_madgear draw order. Colour expansion and sprite flip arithmetic copy MAME's formulas, so on balance the core is mixed.

findings.signal: Priority PROM lookup MAME does not model
findings.note: Layer selection comes from prio_data, indexed by a per-pixel PROM address built from {prio_reg[7], bg_op, obj_pri, fg_op, fg_pen[3], 0, fg_grp, obj_op}. The scrambled pin order and the unused A2 point to board analysis rather than to MAME.

findings.signal: Software priority model transliterates MAME draw order
findings.note: model_sel branches on prio_reg[7] (MAME's m_tilemap_priority & 0x80) and orders sprites by priority class, fg group 1, sprites, fg, bg, following MAME's back-to-front draw calls. It is only reachable through debug_bus[0], so it is a reference model and not the main path.
The LUT is computed as nibble*0x11*(0x10+I)/0x1f, which is exactly MAME's arithmetic. The board would get its levels from a resistor/DAC network instead.

Under flip, Y becomes 240 minus Y and vflip is XORed with flip, matching MAME's 'sy = 240 - sy; flipy = !flipy'. The attribute bits used (0x20 hflip, 0x80 vflip, 0x10 class, 0x0f colour) are the same ones MAME masks.

findings.signal: Sprite scan from last entry to first, per line
findings.note: The per-line state machine walks the buffer from 0xff down to 0, reading the four words. This matches MAME's loop order, but it is a per-scanline line-buffer engine (jtframe_objdraw) and not a per-frame batch, and both priority classes are drawn in one pass, unlike MAME's two.

findings.signal: Sprite buffer copy on vctrl register 4 write
findings.note: A write to register 4 triggers a bulk copy of 1024 words into a local BRAM, the same model as MAME's buffered_spriteram16 copy(). Nothing here models the board's DMA timing.

The chip selects and register slots (fg Y/X, bg Y/X, copy, prio at 0/1/2/3/4/7) match MAME's map. They are written as combinational address compares, not PAL equations; any correct core would share this map.

Both layers are parameterised jtframe_scroll/jtframe_tilemap, with column scan via an index swap (MAME TILEMAP_SCAN_COLS) and tile code/attribute 0x800 words apart. The tile group bit 4 matches MAME's tileinfo.group. Inside there are no board-specific counters or fetch phases.

findings.signal: Interrupts from VBLANK edges with IACK clearing
findings.note: Levels 5/6 are latched on the LVBL edges and cleared by the 68000 FC=7 acknowledge cycle with autovector VPAn, as on a real bus, rather than as HOLD_LINE. Both sides share the levels, so this is weak evidence.
The 512x272 frame with 384x240 visible and blanking/sync points comes from a generic timer's parameters, not from board H/V counter chains. This is ordinary FPGA framework use.
